slides.heading: Largest Range
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Hard · Arrays
slides.narration: Let's solve Largest Range, a hard arrays problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: The problem
bullets: [lo, hi] of the longest run of consecutive integers present in the array.
slides.narration: Here's the problem. lo, hi of the longest run of consecutive integers present in the array.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Only start counting at a number that has no predecessor, so each run is scanned exactly once.
slides.narration: Only start counting at a number that has no predecessor, so each run is scanned exactly once.

slides.heading: Brute force vs optimal
bullets: Sort then scan → O(n log n)
Hash set + only expand from range starts → O(n)
Each number visited at most twice
slides.narration: Sorting and scanning for consecutive runs is n log n. With a hash set, expand only from numbers with no predecessor; each number is touched at most twice, so it's linear.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 1. Put all numbers in a set
2. For each number without number minus one, extend upward
slides.narration: Step by step. First, put all numbers in a set. Second, for each number without number minus one, extend upward. Third, track the longest run's bounds.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Range starting at 0: [0, 7]
slides.narration: 0 has no predecessor, so it starts a range. Walking up gives 0 to 7. The best so far is 0 to 7.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Range starting at 10: [10, 12]
slides.narration: 10 has no predecessor, so it starts a range. Walking up gives 10 to 12. The best so far is 0 to 7.

slides.heading: Worked example
slides.caption: Range starting at 15: [15, 15]
slides.narration: 15 has no predecessor, so it starts a range. Walking up gives 15 to 15. The best so far is 0 to 7.

slides.heading: Java solution
slides.narration: We put everything in a set. For each value with no predecessor, we walk up while the next exists, and keep the widest range.

slides.heading: Complexity
slides.narration: Time is O of n. Space is O of n.

slides.heading: Edge cases & pitfalls
bullets: Only start from range beginnings, or it's O(n²)
slides.narration: If you expand from every number, it's quadratic. Only start where x minus one is missing.

slides.heading: Interview tips & follow-ups
slides.narration: This is the longest consecutive sequence problem.

slides.heading: Recap
bullets: Only start counting at a number that has no predecessor, so each run is scanned exactly once.
slides.narration: To recap Largest Range: Only start counting at a number that has no predecessor, so each run is scanned exactly once. Try re-implementing it from scratch without looking.
